slides.headline: A $28,000 HIV shot now has a $40 version
slides.subline: **The FDA tentatively approved** the first generic of lenacapavir, a long-acting HIV-prevention injection.

slides.body: The FDA gave **tentative approval** to a generic made by **Dr. Reddy's Laboratories**. It is the first generic version of lenacapavir, the HIV-prevention shot from Gilead.
In the US, the branded shot lists at **$28,218 a year**. The generic is expected to cost about [[$40 per person per year]] in lower-income countries.
The approval targets **120 low- and middle-income countries**. Supplies should start to arrive in some places [[within weeks]], though some countries need their own approval first.
One injection can protect a person for months. A price this low could put it in reach of [[millions]] who could not afford it. What medical breakthrough do you want to see next? Tell us below.
